Core OS Software Engineer - USB4/Thunderbolt
Cupertino, CA
Full-time
Onsite
Entry Level
$129K/yr - $225K/yr
Apple is seeking a motivated software engineer to join its Core Operating Systems and Core I/O teams, which develop integrated operating systems and advanced connectivity technologies across Apple devices. The role focuses on implementing USB4 and Thunderbolt protocols, developing kernel driver features, debugging hardware and software interfaces, and collaborating with vendors and cross-functional teams.

Responsibilities
Develop new, innovative Apple products across a fast-paced roadmap
Influence the definition of Apple Silicon and hardware, implementing new features and supporting product bring-up
Contribute to USB4 and Thunderbolt kernel driver extensions across Appleʼs operating systems
Build breakthrough capabilities like RDMA over Thunderbolt, enabling distributed AI inference across clusters of Thunderbolt-connected Macs
Implement new features and enhancements in software as the specifications evolve over time
Debug, root cause, and develop solutions to enhance the USB4 and Thunderbolt customer experience
Collaborate with vendors to drive improvement of the USB4 and Thunderbolt ecosystems, and to ensure interoperability with Appleʼs solutions

Required

Solid foundation in computer science and operating system fundamentals

Preferred
Prior internship, co-op, or university lab experience in systems software, firmware, or embedded development
Familiarity with modern connectivity and high-speed bus architectures (e.g., USB4, Thunderbolt, USB-C/PD, PCIe, or DisplayPort)
Hands-on exposure to driver development concepts or low-level operating systems
Experience using hardware debugging tools (such as protocol analyzers, logic analyzers, or oscilloscopes) to diagnose software/hardware interface issues
Demonstrated ability to trace, debug, and understand multi-layered software systems through school projects, open-source work, or internships
Proactive learner eager to take technical initiative and partner closely with senior mentors and cross-functional teams
